upgrade_contract.current_writes: Emit only the canonical namespace; do not install a second legacy launcher or run a competing state owner.
upgrade_contract.historical_inputs: Explicit upgrade tables and immutable source records identify genuine earlier inputs. They are not current product branding and must not be disguised through encoding or fabricated provenance.
upgrade_contract.database: Bind exact canonical migration definitions to published historical checksums. Preserve original journal times and source bytes. Freeze pre-cutover receipts; aliases may recover only those actual effects, never create new effects under a historical identity.
upgrade_contract.preferences: Move only explicitly owned keys after verified writes. Preserve user values and saved languages. Conflicting authorities retain recovery sources and show a bounded error instead of overwriting.
upgrade_contract.credentials: Authenticate an existing ledger session before cookie transfer. Revoked or invalid tokens cannot migrate. A protocol signing-domain change requires normal authenticated token renewal.
upgrade_contract.execution: Bind actual runtime identities to operation, execution, owner and input before detaching. Missing historical runtime proof is resumable and unconfirmed, never permission to launch a duplicate.
upgrade_contract.environments: Do not move an active or embedded-prefix Conda environment. Validate historical provenance and prepare canonical generations through the existing verified package-cache authority.
upgrade_contract.connector: Preserve extension permissions and origin identity. Transfer existing file capabilities only in the same extension origin and still query actual permissions; a new origin requires normal reauthorization.
upgrade_contract.recovery: After schema 74, use verified forward recovery. An older binary must not open a new schema or overwrite post-cutover user writes with a pre-upgrade backup.
